newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Bank of Korea intervenes again to limit won's fall.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Korea intervenes again to limit won's fall.

text.p: The central Bank of Korea sold dollars again in late Tuesday morning to limit the won's slide against the dollar, dealers said.
They said the BOK intervened at 869.00.
"The won continues falling despite earlier central bank intervention because of rising dollar demand," said a domestic bank dealer.
The won rose slightly to 868.90 minutes after the BOK's dollar sales. It opened at 867.10 and hit an 84-month low of 869.10.
The local currency now hovers at the lowest levels since the market average system was launched in March 1990.
Dealers said widening trade deficit was the main factor for the won's fall. --Seoul Newsroom (822) 727 5645
